query: /devkit:parallel-work 1. Add an Excel download button to the order list screen 2. Add a withdrawal-date field to the member API 3. Show the withdrawal date on the member detail screen
expected_behavior: Checks ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE, HC_TERMINAL_ID and git rev-parse first to choose the launcher and workspace modes, and reads the two matching reference files
Combines 2 and 3 into one worker, or orders 3 after 2 is merged, because 3 uses 2's API result; runs 1 in parallel
Proposes the main repo's current branch as the base branch (or the branch docs/rules/git.md names)
Shows a table with modes, base branch, kind, slug, task branch, scope, parallel/ordered and open points, and creates no worktree before approval
After approval, creates worktrees with python3 -I .../make_worktree.py and launches workers in the format the launcher file gives

query: Fix the 500 error on login failure, investigate which external APIs the payment module calls, and update the README install steps. Run them in parallel
expected_behavior: Classifies the investigation as a read task and runs it in the repo root without a worktree
Uses fix/<slug> for the bug fix and feat/<slug> for the README update (and mentions it if the repo's git rules differ)
The brief forbids commit, push, server start, DB writes and external writes, and states how to report for the chosen launcher

query: If the worker sessions are all done, merge their work and clean up
expected_behavior: Checks each worker's report and the actual git status/diff, shows them in a table, and asks for confirmation before committing
Commits following devkit:commit's rule sources, stages files by name and adds no AI attribution unless the repo rules require it
Records HEAD as the pre-merge point, merges with git merge --no-ff --no-edit, and on conflict runs git merge --abort and reports
Runs the integrated check over git diff --name-only <pre-merge point>..HEAD, with commands from docs/rules or discover.py listed in the confirmation
Cleans up workers, worktrees and branches only after the integrated check and confirmation, and never deletes an unmerged branch

query: (in a plain terminal, neither Orca nor Herdr) Strengthen the payment module unit tests and fix the typos on the admin screen, in parallel
expected_behavior: Finds ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE and HC_TERMINAL_ID empty, tells the user subagents will be used, and reads launcher-subagent.md
After approval, creates worktrees with make_worktree.py and launches both subagents with the Agent tool in one response
The brief includes the line to start every command with 'cd <work folder> &&' and the final-reply report format
Uses no hc or orca commands, and sends fixes with SendMessage

query: (inside an Orca terminal, ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE set) Split the search API pagination and the settings page dark-mode fix and run them at once
expected_behavior: Chooses the orca launcher, reads launcher-orca.md and loads the version-matched guide with `orca skills get orchestration` before any Orca command
After approval, creates one Run and starts each worker with worker-start --spec <brief> --worktree current --agent claude, after making the worktrees with make_worktree.py
Waits with orchestration check --wait and reads each full report with worker-read --source transcript
Does not use the Agent tool or hc for the workers

query: (in ~/scripts, not a git repository) Change the backup script's log path and add a dry-run option to the cleanup script. In parallel
expected_behavior: Finds this is not a git repository and asks whether to run git init before anything else
If declined, uses in-place mode and puts 'no rollback history' and the backup question in the approval table
Runs inplace_snapshot.py snapshot before launching and compares inplace_snapshot.py changed with the reports afterwards
Skips 4-1 to 4-3 and does only the integrated check and cleanup

query: Change the timeout in the config file to 30 seconds
expected_behavior: Does not use parallel-work because this is a single task; edits it directly in this session
Creates no worktree and starts no worker
